edges.description: B-cell autoimmunity can drive antibody and complement injury in the liver.
Humoral autoimmunity also produces Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia.
Complement-associated hepatocyte injury contributes to giant-cell transformation on biopsy.
Pan-lobular complement-mediated hepatocyte necrosis releases hepatic aminotransferases into the circulation.
Acute lobular hepatocyte injury and macrophage-neutrophil inflammation produce hepatic enlargement.
Complement-driven hepatocellular injury impairs bilirubin clearance and contributes to cholestatic jaundice.
Diffuse giant-cell transformation of injured hepatocytes manifests histologically and clinically as giant cell hepatitis.
Progressive hepatocellular damage can lead to liver failure in severe cases.
Loss of lobular architecture and giant-cell hepatitis impair hepatic bilirubin excretion, causing jaundice.
Diffuse giant-cell transformation and hepatic inflammation contribute to liver enlargement.
Immune-mediated red-cell destruction manifests as autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
Acute autoimmune erythrocyte destruction lowers hemoglobin concentration and causes clinical pallor.
Accelerated immune hemolysis increases unconjugated bilirubin load, compounding hepatic jaundice.
Extravascular clearance of antibody-coated erythrocytes in the spleen produces splenomegaly.
Hepatocyte injury is reflected by elevated circulating aminotransferase activity.

evidence.snippet: Widespread complement-mediated hepatocyte injury and typical C3a and C5a complement-driven liver inflammation along with Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia in GCH-AHA provide convincing evidence that systemic B-cell autoimmunity plays a central pathologic mechanism in the disease.
